description: Signature edition. This entry teaches The Future of Employment Law as part of the fundamentals of employment law, presented the Signature way: from first principles, in plain language, building toward mastery. overview: In the Signature teaching of employment law, The Future of Employment Law is a load-bearing idea: understand it and much of the field clicks into place. Wage and hour means minimum wage, overtime, and classification of employees versus contractors. Termination means lawful versus wrongful dismissal. Together these ideas give the learner working intuition, not just vocabulary. The Signature presentation stresses why each principle holds, shows where it is used in real practice, and connects it forward to the Advanced material that follows.

Termination: lawful versus wrongful dismissal.
key_laws: Burden-shifting: the McDonnell Douglas framework proving discrimination.
Just cause: the bargained standard limiting firings in union workplaces.
vocabulary: Hostile work environment: severe or pervasive harassment altering conditions.
Severance: the exit package negotiating departure terms.
methods: Investigation: fair, prompt handling of complaints.
history: Employment law grew from 19th-century master-servant rules; New Deal legislation created modern labor rights. Civil rights laws added anti-discrimination, and the gig economy now tests old categories.
